cands.name: Donnie Chesteen

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican state senator for District 29 since November 2018. Served in the Alabama House (District 87) from 2010 to 2018. Former high school teacher, football coach and athletic director, and former medical sales representative for Mead Johnson. Holds B.S. and M.S. degrees from Troy University.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Chesteen was born or raised, or when he came to Alabama. We found no documented actions or stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no public statements from him on data centers or development. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or endorsements for the 2026 race. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2022 or 2026 candidate surveys. His 2010 campaign website highlighted general support for the economy, education and integrity, but the excerpts did not address these specific issues. The pages did not say which city he lives in.

qual.background: Alabama House member 2010-2018 and state senator since 2018 (about 16 years of legislative service); earlier a high school teacher, football coach and athletic director, and a medical sales representative.
qual.why: Long prior legislative service in both chambers puts him in the high band. The score is held below the top because the record shows no law, policy or budget career outside the legislature. His committee posts and chair were not counted.
